title: XP How customized should a project be?

posts.author: chisaikore
posts.body:
Just wanted to ask as I've got a game in the prototype stage. How much customization should go into a game? I think this would really help with planning & prototyping before moving onto the actual polished version.
To be more specific: this is for RPGMaker XP. It's an older version so I figured I'd specify.
About how custom should
Playable characters
Main or otherwise
NPCs
One time show vs recurring
Tilesets
User interface
Font
Design
Extras (like scripts)
Game mechanics
Scripts
Battle
Anything extra
be? Or in other words, how much of RMXP's default resources in a game is "acceptable"?
The W.I.P games I've seen using XP are gorgeous, but I'm unsure if I can get my own game to that level of quality without some guidelines & planning for myself. Any help would be appreciated, thanks!

posts.author: Ms Littlefish
posts.body:
It really depends on what your goals are.
The RPG Maker user base is pretty diverse in terms of goals and motivations behind making a game with the software. Answering how “acceptable” using the default resources is really depends on how well they align with your goals and motivations.
In a nutshell…they’re acceptable. But, whether you’ll make the game you’re hoping to and achieve certain goals depends on quite a few other factors.

Once again, what game do you want your game to be? Classic turn based? Neat. That's really easy to do. Real time battle? I think there are scripts for that. FPS? Uh, good luck.
Don't add things "just because". Come up with a system first, then see how plausible it is in RPG Maker.

posts.author: Arcaines
posts.body:
Truthfully, 100% of any XP original resource is acceptable.
It wont define how good the game, but it'd be more difficult to stand out a bit more from the other  XP games, unless you do something different with said graphics.

posts.author: midnightzelda
posts.body:
Only you can really decide that. Some things that will affect this are time and money.
If this is your first project I would suggest on trying something small. XP probably has the best looking RTP and you can create amazing games with just that.
Certainly having custom assets will make your game stand out but it takes a lot of time drawing these. If you are not using your time you are probably paying some one else to do it for you. This holds true for the other things such as coding, music, marketing.
You also have to ask yourself whether you are making a commercial game or none commercial game. I am more likely to spend money/time to get customization in my project if I am getting something out of it. Otherwise, it is just not worth all the effort. Free projects are fun I've done a few myself but If it takes longer than 2 years to make, I consider turning it into commercial but that's just me.
If you do everything yourself it is a great learning experience. You will become an artist, coder an storywriter, musician as you learn these things. However it will probably take a very long time to have a playable game at the end of it all.

posts.author: Timeline_man
posts.body:
Ultimately you should do the best of your ability and resources. If you can't make custom animations and can't afford to pay someone to make custom animations, then you'll just have to figure out what you can do within your own limitations.
It is important, especially if you're doing a one-man crew, to know what to prioritize. Doing two hours of pixel art for an NPC that shows up once isn't the most important thing.

posts.author: midnightzelda
posts.body:
Oh hearing that this is your first project is great! I had so much fun learning the engine the first time, I remember I had a notebook full of ideas when I first discovered RPG maker.
Looking back I made just a generic RPG for my first project. It was one town and 4 dungeons. Every project before that I tried doing always ended up in failure. After I did complete my small 4-hour RPG. I had known the system to make a unique looking 40hr RPG experience! Even that one was only meant to be about 10 hours. About a year in I started adding more custom assets and expanding the game. The only one that is important of the bat to be custom is the tileset as that can be hard to change out later. The rest can be placeholders.

posts.author: The_Eerie_One
posts.body:
As others have said it's not about whether it's acceptable but whether it fits what you want. I got nothing against the RTP, but I'm not using most of it in my game just because it doesn't fit the vision for what I want with my game now - but I could definitely see myself making a different game using the RTP later down the road, it looks pretty nice in all honesty. Like the people who made it did a genuinely great job. My biggest fault with it is it just skews too heavily on the fantasy setting and I'm mainly interested in games set in more contemporary times, so it looks like it might be hard to use for what I like but definitely not impossible since there is the SF/science fiction tilesets.
So yeah, think about the game you want to make and how you want it to look like - and if that fits the defaults then yeah nothing wrong at all with using those. And if it doesn't, start looking around for other available assets or be prepared to learn how to create your own.

posts.author: Gilgameshed
posts.body:
You should play some of the free older RPG Maker games to get an idea of what is possible and what limitations there are with the RTP.  A Blurred Line comes to mind, which uses an old RM2K futuristic tile set, and despite the limitations here, ended up turning out really good.  If you can first make a quality and enjoyable project using RTP assets, it will give you more confidence later on to take the plunge into making or hiring people to make custom assets.  Unless you are already very confident in your abilities, I would start with the RTP.  And as others have said, the default assets found in the older generation RPG Makers are nothing short of beautiful, and do match the retro style quite well.
Additionally, for non-commercial projects, there are quite a few free assets available, from sprites to tilesets and more.
Here are two such websites, which I hope I am not breaking any rules by posting.  Unfortunately these assets are generally not viable for commercial projects, but they are great for getting a foothold on things when starting out.
Charas, rpgmaker, the chara generator
